subject: Post-demo: Validate monthly spend band & procurement trigger
messages:
From: Ava Morales <ava@steadyhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@steadyhealth.com>, procurement@steadyhealth.com
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — budget band & PO thresholds

Thanks again for the demo today, Mateo — great walkthrough of the latency/cost controls. A couple quick items I promised to surface after our internal sync: 

- High-level budget range: our team estimates a likely monthly spend between $8k and $45k depending on rollout velocity. That aligns with an initial pilot (lower end) scaling to beta (upper end).
- Procurement rule: anything over $40k/month requires a PO and review by procurement; under that we can entertain a CC + standard SOW.
- Target cost target: our finance director asked for an estimate in $/1M tokens to compare to other vendors — they are hoping for something <= $1,300/1M tokens for the pilot profile.

Can you confirm the unit economics you modeled for the demo prompts (primarily chat + some embedding requests) and whether the $/1M-token figure is achievable within your quantization / batching recommendations? Alsoplease send a short mutual action plan (M.A.P.) we can share with procurement so they know the PO and security materials we'll need.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if it's easier.

Best,
Ava Morales
Senior Product Manager, SteadyHealth
ava@steadyhealth.com

[Attachment: steady_demands_summary.xlsx (Excel, 18KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karl_salesops@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — budget band & PO thresholds

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear notes and for looping procurement. Quick recap from my side and next steps: 

1) Unit economics (pilot profile):
- Modeled token mix: 75% chat generation, 20% short embeddings, 5% batch rerank.
- Estimated unit cost: $1,150 / 1M tokens with recommended settings (8-bit quant + 4-request batching + KV prefix caching). This assumes a sustained median seq length of ~420 tokens per request.
- If you need aggressive cost reduction we can propose a quantized variant (6-bit) that pushes to ~$980 / 1M tokens but may increase a small fraction of hallucination risk on complex prompts.

2) Monthly spend bands (based on your rollout scenarios):
- Pilot (low): $6k - $12k / month (primarily CC-funded, no PO)
- Beta (mid): $12k - $38k / month (preferred to lock a 3-month commit; procurement may request PO depending on internal thresholds)
- Production (high): $38k+ / month (PO + SOW; recommend Redwood Dedicated for predictability)

3) Procurement artifacts I attached: redwood_estimate_v3.pdf (line-item cost by model variant) and a short mutual_action_plan.xlsx that lists the security docs you'll want (SOC 2 summary, redacted audit logs, network diagrams) and approximate RT lead times.

Action items:
- Ava: confirm which band you think fits your initial roll (pilot vs beta) and whether the procurement threshold of $40k is hard or flexible.
- Sam/procurement: if you need a PO for pilot, let us know procurement contact and required PO template so we can align pricing/cycle.
- Mateo/Marissa: schedule a 20-min call later this week if Ava wants a quick pricing walk-through.

If useful I've also added a short one-pager on fallback routing and burst capacity in the estimate.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
T: (415) 555-0193

[Attachment: redwood_estimate_v3.pdf (PDF, 62KB)]

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Ava's ask and my reply. Key points for approval:

- External is expecting a target <= $1,300/1M tokens; I've proposed $1,150 for the pilot using 8-bit quant + batching (estimates attached).
- Procurement threshold at SteadyHealth is ~ $40k/month; if they require PO at the beta band we likely need to propose a 3-month commit to hit procurement comfort and offer a modest commit discount.
- Requested artifacts: SOC2 summary + estimate + mutual action plan. I attached the current estimate.

Questions for you:
- Karthik: are we ok to hold $1,150 as list for the pilot, and do we have authority to offer a 7% commit discount for a 3-mo reserved band?
- Marissa: any objections on the quantized 6-bit alternative as a lower-cost option to present?

I'll wait for your quick reply and will schedule a brief sync only if we need to escalate.

-- Mateo

Mateo — fine to hold $1,150/1M as the pilot list. Approve 7% discount on a 3-month committed band (explicitly for customers that need a PO to approve). Keep the 6-bit option documented but flag QA/quality trade-offs.

Suggested procurement path for SteadyHealth:
- Pilot (< $15k/mo): CC + standard terms; no special procurement.
- Beta ($15k-$40k/mo): encourage a 3-month commit to lock pricing; procurement may accept a mid-size PO after legal sign-off. Offer 7% commit discount if they sign a short reserved commitment.
- Production (>$40k/mo): Enterprise SOW + PO; route to Dedicated offering.

I'll add a HubSpot note and assign the deal to you (RDW-8421).

—Karthik
